historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance and unit growth (~4% selling square footage per year), not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (8.1%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (3.0%) and EPS (2.0%) 3-yr CAGRs. Book equity is distorted by buybacks ($6.7B of treasury stock against $2.7B of equity), so it is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (OCF less gross capex less SBC less equity-award taxes): FY2020 $1,055M, FY2022 $501M, FY2025 $668M. The negative 5-yr figure reflects the FY2020 pandemic working-capital windfall in the base year, not deterioration. EPS is split-adjusted (FY2020 $6.38 pre-split = $1.28). 5-yr revenue CAGR includes the FY2020-21 pandemic step-up; the last three years (3.0%) are the better guide.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands on reaffirmed guidance (sales +3%, adjusted operating margin ~8.65% including ~0.65pp of sale-leaseback gains). FY2027 absorbs the ~$100M tariff-refund lap and diesel/commodity inflation, partly offset by the removal of 74 loss-making Petsense stores, so the underlying margin dips before recovering. Roughly 100 new Tractor Supply stores a year (~4% square footage) with flat-to-slightly-positive comps carries sales growth of 4-4.5% mid-decade, fading to 3% as the store base approaches saturation. Margin rebuilds to the equivalent of a ~9.1% reported operating margin - management's stated aim - but not back to the FY2022-23 peak, because rural competition from Amazon, Walmart and Rural King keeps price investment in place. Allivet and VIP Petcare add modest revenue but are not assumed to lift margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2026 reset proves to be the trough: comps turn sustainably positive (Q3's +0.4% and improving exit rate continue), companion animal recovers with the Allivet/VIP Petcare pet-health ecosystem driving Neighbor's Club engagement, and Project Fusion and garden-centre remodels lift space productivity. Unit growth stays at ~100 stores a year for longer, sales compound 5-6% mid-decade, and fixed-cost leverage plus owned-brand mix restores a reported operating margin near 9.8%. Guidance that analysts already regard as conservative is beaten and the refreshed long-term framework in January 2027 is credible.
scenario_narratives.bear: Comparable sales stay flat-to-negative as Amazon's rural logistics build-out, Walmart and Chewy take share in pet and other commodity categories, and big-ticket seasonal demand remains weak. New stores cannibalise and ramp below chain average, so management slows openings; sales grow only 2-2.5%. Tariff costs, freight and permanent price investment compress gross margin while a larger fixed-cost base deleverages, leaving a reported operating margin near 7.4%. The pet-care acquisitions repeat the Petsense outcome and earn below their cost of capital. The business remains solidly cash-generative and investment grade - this is a margin and growth de-rating, not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tractor Supply is a mature, high-return niche retailer whose value is a steady stream of owner free cash flow after heavy store investment. The valuation rests on three judgments: unit growth of ~4% for several more years, a normalised operating margin a little below the pre-2026 level, and capex net of sale-leaseback proceeds drifting toward depreciation as growth slows. Sale-leaseback gains are stripped from earnings so they are counted once, as cash proceeds. SBC is small (~0.5% of sales with equity-award taxes), so the house and street values are close and the accounting-regime band is narrow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Normalised margin: each 0.5pp of terminal operating margin is worth roughly 6-7% of value; the FY2027 tariff-refund lap and the unpublished new long-term framework make this the least certain input
Sale-leaseback dependence: ~$250M a year of proceeds and ~$90-100M of booked gains depend on continued owned-store development; if the programme slows, net capex rises and reported margins fall
Operating leases of $4.4B are excluded from net debt and charged as rent; they are real fixed obligations that amplify the bear case
Unit growth saturation arriving earlier than modelled, or new-store cannibalisation holding comps negative
FY2026 working-capital absorption (inventory, tax receivable) not reversing
Terminal value is capped at a multiple in all scenarios (Gordon at 8% WACC exceeds the cap), so value is sensitive to the cap choice rather than to terminal growth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 28.36-56.28
data_sources.financials: TSCO_Metrics.csv / TSCO.duckdb (SEC XBRL); FY2025 10-K (capex split, sale-leaseback gains, SBC, tax rate); Q3 FY2026 10-Q for the period ended 2026-09-26 (debt, cash, finance leases, share count, 9M cash flow, guidance)
data_sources.qualitative: TSCO_Analysis.json dated 2026-11-15 (Petsense restructuring, guidance history, competitive position, bull/bear cases)

inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 518.574M shares outstanding at 2026-10-24 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover) plus ~0.9M dilutive share-based awards (Q3 FY2026 EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC and equity-award taxes are expensed in the flows. The ~110M shares_outstanding values in the Q1/Q2 2023 CSV rows are a pre-split XBRL glitch and were not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense $57.1M plus $15.9M cash taxes on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities). The filer publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~0.8 for a needs-based, investment-grade (Baa1/BBB) retailer -> cost of equity ~8.3%. After-tax cost of debt ~4.1% (5.20%-5.25% recent senior notes, 22% tax) at ~10% of capital -> ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios; risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is an operating expense inside EBITDA, so the lease cost is charged in the flows and the $4.43B of operating lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. Finance lease liabilities ($58.0M) are included in total_debt. No separate lease_cost_pct_path is needed.
inputs.sale_leaseback_treatment: TSCO books gains on sale-leaseback of owned stores inside SG&A ($93.1M in FY2025, $81.8M in 9M FY2026, ~0.6% of sales). The gain is not operating earnings; its cash arrives in investing as sale proceeds. To count it once, ebitda_margin_path EXCLUDES the gain and capex_pct_path is capex NET of sale-leaseback proceeds (management's own guidance basis: $675-700M for FY2026). Reported operating margins are therefore ~0.6pp higher than the EBIT margins implied here.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods routing: US operating company, consumer retail). Fresh build, no prior valuation. FY0 is FY2025 (last audited year); year 1 is FY2026, which is ~10.5 months elapsed at the valuation date and is anchored to guidance reaffirmed on 2026-10-22 (net sales +2.5-3.5%, adjusted operating margin 8.5-8.8%, net capex $675-700M). Because year 1 is discounted a full period and net debt is the September 2026 balance, the timing is modestly conservative (roughly 4-5% of value). reported_fcf is operating cash flow less gross capex ($1,635.3M - $894.8M); sale-leaseback proceeds of $256.1M are excluded from it. Buybacks are funded ($361.3M in FY2025, $342.7M in 9M FY2026), so the flat share count is paid for in cash, not a convention. Interest income is nil; the company is in net debt. Year-1 modelled FCF does not capture the unusual FY2026 working-capital absorption (inventory +$530M and income taxes receivable +$169M in 9M), part of which is seasonal and should reverse.
inputs.known_limitations: The FY2026 adjusted operating margin embeds roughly $100M of tariff refunds that management says will not recur in FY2027; the base case removes them in year 2. A refreshed long-term framework is promised with Q4 FY2026 results (late January 2027) and is the main scheduled evidence that would move the margin and growth paths.

bear.margin_note: EBIT ex-gain slides to 6.8% (reported ~7.4%) as comps stay negative on a growing fixed-cost base and price investment becomes permanent.

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin_path = EBIT ex sale-leaseback gains + D&A + SBC expense (0.41%). EBIT ex-gain path: 8.0% (FY2026 guide 8.65% adjusted less ~0.65% gain), 7.6% (tariff-refund lap), 7.8, 8.0, 8.2, 8.4, then 8.5% - equivalent to a reported operating margin of ~9.1%, matching management's aim of 'above 9% over time' and below the FY2025 9.45%.
base.capex_note: Net of sale-leaseback proceeds. 4.3% in FY2026 per guidance, drifting to 3.5% as unit growth slows; terminal capex sits just above D&A.
base.tax_note: Effective rate 21.6% FY2025, 22.1% FY2024; 22% held flat. FY2025 cash taxes were low on OBBBA timing, which is not carried forward.
base.wc_note: Inventory + prepaids less payables and accruals is ~7% of sales; growth consumes cash.

bull.margin_note: EBIT ex-gain recovers to 9.2% by year 6 (reported ~9.8%, between FY2025's 9.45% and the FY2022-23 peak of ~10.2%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: comps were negative for most of FY2026, management withdrew its long-term framework, and it has already flagged FY2027 margin headwinds, while structural rural competition is intensifying; there is no balance-sheet or solvency risk, so it is not higher. Base 50%: reaffirmed guidance, a visible store pipeline and a stated margin goal make the middle path the most likely. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs a comp recovery, margin restoration and a successful pet-health platform together, and the last small-format pet bet (Petsense) failed.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
